text.sourceText: To find the y-intercept of a linear equation:
1. Rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form with the y-term on     one side of the equation and the x-term and constant term on the other.     (This step has already been done.)
2. If the y-term is multiplied by a number, divide every term by that number.     (This step is not needed for this problem.)
3. The y-intercept is the constant term.
